display.purpose: Big titles in the stage voice: Set complete, Paused, Calibrate, the song title on results and in the song sheet. Balanced wrap.

page-title.purpose: One per screen: Pick a set, Music library, Ready up, Settings.

wordmark.purpose: The product name on Home only, with a pink glow behind it. A working title; nothing depends on it.

tile-title.purpose: Names of set tiles on Home.

panel-title.purpose: Panel headings (Setlist, the settings detail card). Settings section headings are 1.15rem, the highlighted song 1.2rem.

score.purpose: The results score and the set total, counting up. Tabular figures, not uppercased. HUD score is clamp(26px, 2.3vw, 54px).

stat.purpose: Values in result stat cells. The hold button label is the same voice at 1.3rem.

control.purpose: Buttons, action-bar actions, tabs and option names.

label.purpose: Names a group of controls inside a panel: Part, Difficulty, Listen, Best scores, Next up. Ink 2.

item-title.purpose: Song names in rows, slots and set cards; one line with ellipsis. Setting names are the same size at weight 700.

body.purpose: Artists (0.95rem), help text, hints and errors (line-height 1.45, max 62ch).

caption.purpose: Stat captions and best-score table heads. The smallest text in the interface. Ink 3.

rootFontSize.purpose: Every menu size is rem off this root, so the interface grows with the window and with the player's interface-size setting (85% to 130%). The HUD is in px.

inputVariants.attribute: data-input on the root element: mouse | keyboard | pad | touch, set from the last input used
inputVariants.mouse: Keycap hints; hover styles; no focus ring; a pause button during play.
inputVariants.keyboard: Keycap hints; the travelling focus ring; arrow keys move focus, Q and E switch tabs.
inputVariants.pad: Controller symbols as hints, plus a passive Select hint in the action bar; the travelling focus ring; D-pad or left stick move focus, shoulder buttons switch tabs.
inputVariants.touch: No hints (action icons show instead); targets 3rem, small buttons, step arrows and the search clear button 2.75rem; action bar 4.5rem; step arrows and row details always visible; during play the lanes are the controls and the HUD moves to the top and sides.

motionPreference.attribute: data-motion on the root element: full | reduced (the player's setting, or the system preference when the setting is System)
motionPreference.reduced: All animation and transition durations drop to 0.01ms except hit feedback, the countdown and the break ring; the ring's bounces are removed and the countdown fades without scaling; tiles do not lift; score count-ups show the final value.

shadows.name: ring-glow
shadows.purpose: Under the travelling focus ring (with outline: 3px solid var(--mint); outline-offset: 3px).

shadows.name: dialog
shadows.purpose: Sheets and cards over the dimmed screen.

shadows.name: lane-underline
shadows.purpose: The lane colour of a bound key (4px on settings caps). The same inset in gold marks a full combo in the best-scores table.

shadows.name: sticky-start
shadows.purpose: The hold button when it sticks to the foot of the ready panel on phones.

shadows.name: countdown-glow
shadows.purpose: Behind the countdown numbers before a song.

shadows.name: overdrive-glow
shadows.purpose: The overdrive meter when it can be used or is running.

shadows.name: veil
shadows.value: radial-gradient(70% 46% at 78% -6%, rgb(93 242 214 / 0.2), transparent 70%), radial-gradient(60% 50% at 12% -10%, rgb(124 92 255 / 0.4), transparent 70%), linear-gradient(180deg, rgb(14 8 40 / 0.86), rgb(26 14 84 / 0.66) 46%, rgb(14 8 40 / 0.9))
shadows.purpose: The night between the stage and the panels, with the aurora band across the top. 72% opacity on Ready up, Results and the summary.

motion.name: ease-in
motion.purpose: Dialogs leaving and the launch wipe closing.

motion.name: ring-glide
motion.value: 200ms on transform, width, height and radius; fade 0.16s
motion.purpose: The focus ring travelling between controls.

motion.name: scene-forward
motion.purpose: Going deeper. Settings tab lists use the same at 0.35s.

motion.name: rise-in
motion.value: from translateY(0.9rem), opacity 0; tiles 0.5s at i * 55ms + 60ms; set cards 0.45s at i * 60ms + 80ms; song rows 0.4s at i * 22ms + 60ms (first 12)

motion.name: slot-in
motion.purpose: A song landing in a setlist slot. Its badge pops from scale 0.4 in 0.35s.

motion.name: tile-lift
motion.purpose: A set tile under focus or the mouse.

motion.name: dialog-in
motion.value: dim 0.22s; side sheet from translateX(3rem) 0.34s; phone sheet from translateY(2.5rem); card from translateY(1rem) scale(0.96) 0.3s

motion.name: hold-fill
motion.value: 650ms to full; drains 6% per frame when let go

motion.name: launch-wipe
motion.value: three sheets (pink, violet, night) as clip-path circles from 50% 100% in 0.55s, 60ms apart; hold at least 620ms; close toward 50% 0% in 0.5s ease-in, reverse order 50ms apart

motion.name: results-reveal
motion.value: stars 0.55s from scale(0.3) rotate(-25deg), from 250ms, 140ms apart; score count-up 1.3s (set total 1.4s after 300ms); tags at 1.2s; stat cells from 0.7s, 45ms apart

motion.name: hud-star-earn
motion.purpose: A star disc as it is earned.

motion.name: hud-break
motion.value: bounce 0.55s cubic-bezier(0.25, 1.6, 0.45, 1) on each bar; beat 0.3s; number tick 0.5s cubic-bezier(0.2, 1.4, 0.4, 1)

motion.name: hud-countdown
motion.purpose: Each countdown number before a song.

feedback.sounds: Short orchestral recordings in the menu theme's key, with their own volume: move, select, back, tab, toggle-on, toggle-off, launch, star, count, best, pause, resume, error, add, cheer, applause. One shared handler gives every control its move and select sound; a control picks another with data-sfx (back, tab, launch, none). During play only the pause menu sounds.

rumble.name: tab-left / tab-right
rumble.value: amp 0.45, 40ms, click fully on the side moved toward

feedback.rumbleScope: Only on the controller in use, scaled by the rumble setting; native haptics on controllers that support them.

breakpoints.name: folded
breakpoints.purpose: Library setlist becomes a dock; settings detail pane folds into the highlighted row; Ready up and Results go to one column.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Home tiles stack as rows; secondary actions shrink to icons; dialogs rise from the foot; setting rows stack; the hold button sticks to the foot of its panel.

breakpoints.name: short
breakpoints.purpose: Tighter head and a 3.5rem action bar; Home drops its page title.

breakpoints.name: phone-sideways
breakpoints.purpose: Ready up and Results stay side by side.

layout.actionBar: 4.1rem (4.5rem on touch, 3.5rem on short screens), plus the bottom safe area
layout.layers: dialogs 20 (30 during play), action bar 40, toasts 60, drop target 65, focus ring 70, launch wipe 80
layout.hudUnits: px with vw clamps, positioned from --hw-x, --hw-y, --hw-w and --lane-w, which the highway publishes

highway.deck: Solid violet, rgb(18 10 48) near the player to rgb(29 16 79) at the far end, 96.5% opaque and fading out over the far 40%; hairlines between lanes; neighbouring lanes 7% apart in tone.
highway.rails: Lit violet (#bd78ff) along both edges and as a lip across the front; blue in overdrive.
highway.tiles: Rounded pills (0.82 by 0.32 lane widths): rim in the lane colour lit 30% toward white, top face in the lane colour, a white gloss line. Missed tiles dim to 28%.
highway.strikeTargets: A pill outline per lane in its colour, dark (#100828) inside; finger-sized rounded squares on touch (--pads: square).
highway.laneLight: A played lane lights along its length in its own colour, brightest at the player's end.
highway.strikeLine: --strike on the highway canvas: 0.775 of its height; 0.992 on touch. The strike line spans 43% of a wide screen and up to 80% of a tall one.

components.name: Primary Action (Ready up)
components.description: The one pink step forward on a screen or dialog, as it sits in the action bar with the keycap hint a keyboard player sees. Text on pink is Pink Ink.

components.name: Button

components.description: A problem notice above the action bar: a plum card with a Pink Light alert icon that rises in, and is dismissed on press or after 6s.

narrative.northStar: The Night Sky Over the Stage
narrative.overview:
The menus are the night sky over an open-air stage. The live 3D stage idles behind every screen, a veil of deep indigo and violet lies over it with a faint band of aurora light across the top, and the interface floats in front as rounded violet sheets. One aurora-mint ring is the player's place on the screen: it travels from control to control as they move with the keyboard or a controller, taking each control's size and corner radius as it lands. What the player has chosen is a pale lavender sheet with dark ink on it, and when the choice changes that sheet slides to the new item. Hot pink is the single step forward on a screen. Gold is only ever something the player earned. The player's own cover art carries most of the colour; the panels stay violet so the covers and the one pink action read first.

The type does the shouting. Archivo is set wide, black, leaning and uppercase for titles, tile names and numbers; at normal width, leaning and uppercase for control labels; and at normal width and upright for everything a player reads as a sentence. Everything is rounded: three radii for sheets and controls, full circles for icon buttons, badges and the HUD's dials. Sizes are in rem off a root that grows with the window and is multiplied by the player's own interface-size setting, so the same layout reads on a phone, at a desk and from across a room.

The interface is built for four inputs and shows the one in use. The root element carries `data-input` (mouse, keyboard, pad or touch), set from the last input the player used, and the interface changes variant with it: keycaps or controller symbols as hints, hover or the travelling ring, larger targets under a finger. During play the menu world steps back: the HUD is quiet chrome around the highway, and nothing in it moves for decoration.
keyCharacteristics: Layered violet night: indigo ground, a violet glow rising from below, the live stage behind a veil, an aurora band across the top.
Rounded violet sheets (0.45, 0.75 and 1.1rem radii) with no borders and no shadow at rest.
Four light roles that never trade places: pink acts, mint is the focus ring, lavender with dark ink is the selection, gold is earned.
One focus ring and one selection sheet per group, and both travel instead of blinking.
Lane colours are data (lane, difficulty, multiplier level, key binding), not decoration.
One family, three registers: wide black italic uppercase, normal-width italic uppercase for controls, normal-width upright for reading.
Variants by last input: hints, hover, focus ring, target size and play layout all follow `data-input`.
Every interaction has a sound; on a controller it also has a pulse. `data-motion='reduced'` keeps state changes and drops travel.

rules.name: The One Ring Rule
rules.body: Mint is focus. In a menu it never fills a control, marks a choice, labels a status or decorates; it is the travelling ring, the caret, and the one faint aurora band in the sky.

rules.name: The One Pink Rule
rules.body: A screen or dialog has at most one pink button at rest, and it is the step forward. Everything else is violet or quiet. A selected item is never pink.

rules.name: The Lavender Rule
rules.body: A choice is shown by a pale lavender sheet with dark ink, never by pink, mint or an outline. Focus and selection on the same item show both: the lavender sheet with the mint ring around it.

rules.name: The Lanes Are Data Rule
rules.body: A lane colour always means a lane, a difficulty level or a multiplier level. Never use one as a brand accent or a decorative stripe.

rules.name: The Three Registers Rule
rules.body: A title or a number is wide, black, italic and uppercase. A control label is normal width, italic and uppercase. Anything read as a sentence, and every song and artist name, is normal width, upright and in its own case. Never set a sentence in the stage voice.

rules.name: The Root Scale Rule
rules.body: The root size is `clamp(16px, 0.62vw + 7px, 26px)` multiplied by the player's interface-size setting (`--ui-scale`, 85% to 130%). Every menu size is in rem, so the whole interface grows with the window and with the player's choice. Only the HUD is in px.

rules.name: The Flat Sheets Rule
rules.body: Nothing has a shadow at rest. A panel is a fill; a row is a lighter fill; a well is a darker one. Shadow is reserved for the ring, the selection, and things that float over a screen.

rules.name: The Lit State Rule
rules.body: Focus is the ring plus the control's own lit state: a row brightens to Lit Row, a set tile rises 0.4rem and brightens to Raised Violet. Under the mouse the control shows the same lit state without the ring.

dos: **Do** build surfaces as flat rounded violet sheets: Panel Violet at 1.1rem for panels and tiles, Row at 0.75rem for list rows, Well for recessed troughs and fields.
**Do** keep the four light roles: pink for the one forward action, mint for the focus ring, a lavender sheet with dark ink for the selection, gold for what was earned.
**Do** let focus be the one travelling ring plus the control's own lit state, and show it only for keyboard and controller players.
**Do** move selection with one travelling lavender sheet per group (0.36s, `--ease`) rather than toggling each item's fill.
**Do** use lane colours only to mean lane, difficulty or multiplier level.
**Do** put a screen's actions in the action bar with a key and, where it makes sense, a controller button, and let the hint follow `data-input`: keycap, controller symbol, or none on touch.
**Do** gate hover styles behind `data-input='mouse'` and raise targets to at least 2.75rem under `data-input='touch'`.
**Do** size menus in rem off the clamped root, and the HUD in px over the highway's geometry.
**Do** set titles and numbers wide, black, italic and uppercase; control labels at normal width, italic and uppercase; sentences and song names at normal width and upright.
**Do** give every new control a sound through the shared handler (`data-sfx` for back, tab, launch or none) and its matching controller pulse.
**Do** make every new entrance, stagger or travel respect `data-motion='reduced'`, keeping the state change.
**Do** keep the HUD still except for gameplay feedback.
donts: **Don't** use mint for anything in the menus except the focus ring and the caret: no mint fills, borders, badges, status or decoration.
**Don't** put more than one pink button on a screen or dialog at rest, and don't mark a selected item in pink.
**Don't** put borders or resting shadows on panels, rows or buttons; the only strokes are hairline dividers and dashed "empty" outlines.
**Don't** skew or square off shapes; the italic type is the only slant.
**Don't** use a lane colour as a brand accent or a decorative stripe.
**Don't** set sentences or song names in the stage voice, or controls in the upright reading voice.
**Don't** show hover effects, key hints or the focus ring to a touch player.
**Don't** animate anything in the HUD for decoration, or let menu motion run during play.
**Don't** let a layout depend on the product name: the wordmark "Soundwave" is set in type, not drawn into the design.
**Don't** name, imitate or recreate any existing commercial rhythm game in look, copy, assets or layout.
